Apertus-Recht: which racial-discrimination law does Apertus apply?

People ask chat assistants whether something they said is punishable. We release 1,980 German, French and Italian scenarios under Art. 261bis StGB, built as minimal twins that change one legal fact at a time. Intent and the dignity threshold are stipulated, so the set tests how a model applies the elements, not whether it predicts a conviction. Each verdict is computed by code from pinned Fedlex texts and agrees with 57 of 57 Swiss court rulings we could code. Without the law, Apertus v1.5 70B convicts every German scenario and, in free text, calls 73 of 75 lawful ones punishable. Rules spelled out in plain sentences make it apply the publicity rule, but not the closed list of protected groups or the date the article took effect. Pasting the verbatim law undoes even that. A second statute fails in another shape. One command re-derives every label and number.

Track: Apertus Readiness · Track 1B (Swiss Voices, behavioural alignment) · Event: Online · Team: 444
Demo: https://apertus-recht.mi11ion.io (every scenario, its gold and Apertus's answers) · make run (Docker, CPU, no key)

Use of Apertus

  • Model: Apertus v1.5 70B; Apertus v1.5 8B (public Q4_K_M GGUF; for exploration also the SFT, RLVR, DPO and final stages, bf16 blends, Q8_0 and MLX 4-bit builds).
  • How it is used: evaluation only: forced choice, preference pairs, and free text read by three blind judges.
  • Where it runs: the 70B on Public AI through a cost-capped gateway. Public AI's name apertus-v1.5-8b currently serves the 70B (same output as -70b on 760 of 792 test prompts, docs/builds.md), so every hosted number is the 70B. The 8B runs as the public GGUF on CPU in GitHub Actions.
  • Links: code https://github.com/mi11ione/apertus-recht · dataset https://huggingface.co/datasets/mi11ion/apertus-recht

Use Case Description

Art. 261bis StGB punishes racial discrimination; since 1 July 2020 it also covers sexual orientation. Whether a statement is punishable turns on three elements a layperson cannot check:

  • Publicity. Under BGE 130 IV 111 E. 5.2, statements among family, friends or in a setting of personal trust are not public.
  • The closed list. Only race, ethnicity, religion and sexual orientation are protected.
  • The date. The article entered into force on 1 January 1995; sexual orientation is covered from 1 July 2020.

A wrong answer misinforms people about their own speech, in either direction. The users are Swiss residents asking an assistant in German, French or Italian, with or without the law in context (Apertus-v1.5-8B: 698,641 downloads in the 30 days before 9 October 2026). The article was adopted by referendum in 1994 and extended by referendum in 2020; Apertus's training data contain BGE 130 IV 111 verbatim. The dataset asks not "how often is the model right" but which law it applies, element by element.

Dataset Summary

Per language: 660 scenarios in 220 twin groups (220 base, 215 true flips, 210 placebos, 15 contested); verdicts 430 convict, 215 acquit, 15 open. Each scenario has an acceptance criterion, an item-specific chosen answer, a rejected answer and a length-matched mirror, a settled or contested label, its normative source and its element-by-element derivation. The 660 German scenarios are also retold in the first person (de_lay).

Term Meaning
Twin a variant that changes exactly one fact of its base. A true flip changes the verdict; a placebo does not.
Rung how much law the prompt carries. R0 no law · R3 rules spelled out (the elements, a one-sentence paraphrase of BGE 130 IV 111, the closed list) · R4 R3 plus one sentence on the 2020 extension · R5 verbatim law (Fedlex text of Art. 261bis and Art. 2 StGB, the Regeste) · R6 R5 with an instruction to check each element
Framing how the verdict is asked: Ja/Nein, or the verdict word ("Urteil: schuldig / nicht schuldig")
Misapplied (red) the model convicts a variant the law acquits, while it convicts the unchanged base (95% intervals)
Read-back the law the model applies, element by element, read off the twins
Family (groups per language) One-fact change of the base Tests
SET (55) public → private setting; placebo: family wording of a public statement BGE 130 IV 111 E. 5.2
CHAR (60), CHARX (20) protected → unprotected characteristic; placebo: synonym ("Hautfarbe", "Glaube") closed list
DATE_SO (35) sexual orientation 2021–25 → before 1 Jul 2020; placebo: 1 Jul / Aug 2020 AS 2020 1609, Art. 2 StGB
DATE_CTRL (25) race, ethnicity, religion → 2018–20 (placebo) and → 1993/94 over-application; entry into force
CONTESTED (15) public → fact-dependent setting (gold open) hedging
WORDING (10) another wording family; another paragraph wording invariance

Unprotected characteristics: gender identity, sex, canton, occupation, age, disability, political opinion. The wording is templated (18 act wordings, 29 settings, 33 group phrases; 44 words on average): that is the price of exact twins.

What is new. To our knowledge no dataset lets one test which version of a real statute a model applies, element by element, in the three official languages (sources in docs/prior-art.md):

Dataset Languages Gold One-fact twins Real amendment dates Checked against courts
LEXam / SwissLegalEvals DE, EN / DE, FR, IT exam keys, LLM judges no no no
LawShift (NeurIPS 2025) ZH expert metamorphic relations yes hypothetical revisions no
TALD (2026) ZH statute version cited in judgments no which version applies from judgments
OpenExempt (2026) EN solver over expert encodings single-factor suites one deadline rule no
Multilingual HateCheck DE, FR, IT, … by construction templated contrasts no (not legal) no
Apertus-Recht DE, FR, IT code from pinned Fedlex texts yes, with placebos 1995, 2020, Art. 2 StGB 57/57 rulings

Data Collection Method

No data was collected from people. A seeded generator renders the scenarios from YAML templates. A 97-line engine computes each verdict from a machine-readable element model of the statute (statutes/stgb_261bis/statute.yaml). Every element cites a pinned source: the Fedlex texts of Art. 261bis before and since 1 July 2020 and of Art. 2 StGB in three languages (sha256 of each text), the amendment footnotes, and the Regeste of BGE 130 IV 111. The engine, not the author, labels each variant a true flip, a placebo or contested; the generator refuses to build if that disagrees with the design. French and Italian were translated by Claude agents with the official terms, back-translated blind (0 critical findings) and localised by a lawyer-persona review (places in Romandie and Ticino, Swiss formulas).

Verification without human labels. Because gold is computed, review looks for errors in the code, the element model or the wording. Every review step was done by Claude agents working blind on opaque ids, without code or gold.

  • Annotation: six agents labelled 960 items; they agree with the code on 939/939 settled items and name the deciding element in 315/315 acquittals. A second pass that saw only the law agreed on 939/939. A model of another family (Qwen), given the same law-only task, agrees on 910/939; each of its 29 disagreements convicts a case the pinned text does not cover (pre-2020 sexual orientation, pre-1995, unlisted characteristics): Apertus's own errors, not gold errors (A15).
  • Adjudication: two independent adjudicators reviewed every disagreement, every contested item and a blind 10% sample. Gold was wrong in 0 of 94 sampled items.
  • Court validation: 326 decisions citing Art. 261bis were triaged and coded twice (κ 0.83–0.98). The engine agrees with 57/57 in-scope rulings, 52/52 distinct cases (repeat instances merged, Perinçek left out as revised after Strasbourg). This tests the conviction rules well and the acquittal rules thinly: an engine that always convicts would score 55/57. One of the two acquittals is clean; one agrees on another ground (A15).
  • Wording fixes: two defects were found before any result was analysed (A3) and four after (A5). All were fixed and re-scored; the pre-fix responses are archived.

Dataset Details

Quality gates (statute-twins qc, all passing): schema; gold recomputed for every item; twin invariants; no duplicates; language identity; canary; a PII scan of items, responses and metadata (0 hits). Tests check every closed-list term and both in-force dates against the official text in three languages. Mutation tests (drop religion from the list, move the 2020 date by a day, make private settings public) flip exactly the items each rule governs.

Contamination. None of our 35,241 distinct 13-grams occurs in the 1,069,365 decisions of voilaj/swiss-caselaw; the same scan finds 846 of the 1,525 13-grams of the statute and the Regeste (positive control).

Ethics and licensing. No data subjects: generic actors, groups named by their characteristic, abstract acts. CDLA-Permissive-2.0 with per-item licence components; statute and decision texts are public domain (Art. 5 URG). A consent form with an AI-use clause is ready for human reviewers. Every item carries a canary string.

Evaluation

Three measurements on one item set.

  • Forced choice (all items, R0 to R5, two framings): the log-probability of the convicting answer minus the acquitting one, exact on vLLM (prefilled answer), from the logits in llama.cpp.
  • Preference (settled items, R0): the same scoring between each item's chosen answer and its mirror, the same sentence with the verdict and the deciding legal claim negated (median length ratio 1.0).
  • Free text (the same 240 items in each language, R0, R3, R5, greedy): each answer is judged against its acceptance criterion by three blind judges. Two are Claude judges; they agree on 718 of 720 pass decisions (κ 0.993), which measures self-consistency of one model. The independent judge is Qwen-SEA-LION-v4-32B: it agrees with their consensus on 694 of 718 (κ 0.73 on acquittal and open items). A deterministic parser of each answer's verdict agrees on 698 of 700 settled answers. A seeded 20% sample is laid out for a human check.

The read-back. Each true flip is paired with its base, which the statute convicts. With 95% item-bootstrap intervals of the mean log-odds of conviction, an element is misapplied when both lie above zero. A framing in which the base itself is not convicted cannot be read. The pre-registered test fits the read-back on two wording families and predicts the third; it passes if it beats the statute by at least 0.15 in every readable framing.

Runs. The 70B on Public AI (vLLM, temperature 0) in three languages at R0 to R5; the 8B public Q4_K_M GGUF (sha256 a037df8d…) on CPU CI runners, German R0 to R5; preference on 645 settled items per language; free text on 720 answers per language; Art. 179ter (120 items); the 162-item battery for training stages. Every row records the served model and a request hash.

Results

Without the law, the 70B convicts everything. At R0 the recall of acquittals is at most 0.01 in every language and framing. The model is not blind to the facts: its scores still rank punishable above lawful cases (AUC 0.72–0.77). But the threshold sits so far on the convicting side that no case falls below it. Asking the other way round ("would a court acquit?") changes nothing: 0 of 215 acquittals in every language, so this is not a bias towards "yes". In free text the judges fail 73 of 75 answers to lawful scenarios as misleading; every one names Art. 261bis. The independent judge alone counts 72.

With the rules spelled out (R3), publicity is applied; the closed list and the date are not. Figure 1 shows each element for the German 70B:

  • Private settings are acquitted. Every private variant names family or friends, the words of the paraphrase, so this shows uptake of a stated example more than application of BGE 130 IV 111.
  • Canton, disability and political opinion stay red: convicted although the prompt lists the four protected characteristics. Gender identity is applied once the prompt names it as excluded.
  • The R3 gain is fragile. Asked whether a court would acquit, the 70B also acquits half the punishable cases, and its scores rank the cases backwards (AUC 0.27). Averaged over both question directions, private settings still hold; most other acquittals do not (Table 3).
  • The date sentence (R4) backfires. One sentence saying that sexual orientation is protected since 1 July 2020 makes the 70B acquit the earlier cases, but also stop convicting punishable cases from 2021–25: 0 of 35 with the verdict word in German. The 8B convicts 14 of 35 with Ja/Nein (19 with the verdict word). The sentence does not teach the date; it takes the characteristic off the list.
  • Acts from 1993/94, before the article entered into force, are convicted at every rung. No rung states the 1995 date, so this is a gap in what the model knows.

The verbatim law (R5) undoes the rules. Given the Fedlex text and the Regeste, as a retrieval pipeline would paste them, the German 70B convicts everything again: 0 of 215 acquittals with Ja/Nein, 1 with the verdict word. In French and Italian it recognises 12 and 43, against 120 and 97 with the rules spelled out. In free text, 75 of 75 answers to lawful scenarios call them punishable. The scores do register the facts (a private setting lowers the conviction score by 6.6 nats, from 14.7), but never below the threshold. No single part of the law text explains it (Table 3).

Recognising the law is not applying it. Shown an item's correct answer and its mirror, the 70B picks the correct one (German 0.98), most cleanly in the closed-list and date columns, although its own verdicts convict those cases. In French it prefers the mirror for half the punishable cases (0.53); we have not isolated why.

Pre-registered held-out test. At R0 it passes trivially: a model that convicts everything is predicted perfectly. At R3 and R4 the read-back beats the statute in every cell, but not by the pre-registered 0.15 in every framing. The test fails, and by our rule these rungs report Figure 1, not the read-back. Two cells could not pass at all, and the split varies only the wording, so it tests wording invariance.

Post-training and builds (8B, 162-item battery; one checkpoint pair, so a lead): RLVR → DPO cuts correct acquittals under stated rules from 185 to 146 of 220 while keeping 104/104 convictions. The public Q8_0 GGUF agrees with bf16 on 638 of 648 decisions, the Q4_K_M on 622, our MLX 4-bit conversion on 548.

Dataset Limitations

  • Depth over breadth. One statute modelled exactly, three of its five paragraphs. Intent, the characteristic and the dignity threshold are stated in the facts, where most court acquittals turn, so the set measures element application, not conviction prediction. A second statute (Art. 179ter) is released in the same five-file format.
  • Exact twins need controlled wording. The first-person retelling shows the findings hold outside the charge-sheet register.
  • Two contestable legal choices, stated. An Abs. 2 act ("propagating an ideology") is also told as a one-off statement; an online post before 1 July 2020 counts as completed on publication (dropping those items moves no accuracy by more than 1.4 points).
  • Every review is re-runnable: agent runs with their instructions in the repository, no private human judgment in the gold. One model family's blind spots are checked from outside it: the gold against the official text, mutation tests and court decisions; the free text by an independent judge and a parser.
  • Contested items are few (15 per language). Accuracy intervals treat items as independent; held-out gains use twin-group bootstraps.

Lessons Learnt and Recommendations

  • Users: do not ask about Art. 261bis without the law in context, and do not count on pasting the statute. State the rule the case turns on in a plain sentence, and check the characteristic and the date yourself. Prefer the Q8_0 GGUF or the served model to 4-bit MLX conversions.
  • Developers: in our one checkpoint pair, DPO costs acquittals under stated rules (8B: 185 → 146 of 220). The model obeys exclusions it is told but not "the list is closed", and reads plain rules but not the law as written: instruction-following and long-context legal reading are training targets. Keep the chosen / rejected pairs out of training if you evaluate on them.

Reproducibility

make run (Docker, CPU, no key, no model) regenerates the dataset from the YAML (sha256 per file), recomputes every result from the stored responses, checks every request hash against its prompt, re-aggregates the judges, checks the pre-registration (prereg-verify: locked files, amendments A1–A15, the frozen held-out code) and the claims.tsv numbers for both statutes, and exits non-zero on any mismatch. LLM_* variables or make run-gguf add a live slice. Seeds: generator 261, bootstrap 0 (2,000 resamples). License: code Apache-2.0; dataset CDLA-Permissive-2.0; this report CC-BY-4.0.
